T.pageTitle: Keep Watch - Community Builders of Pecan Grove
T.introBuilt: It's spring, one year later. The town said yes to the data center, with changes.
T.introStudying: It's spring, one year later. The town said not now. It's still studying and writing rules.
T.fair: Saying yes with changes and saying not now, to study more, are both fair choices. Either way, people made promises. Let's check them, kindly.
T.s1: Read the promise. Tap its clue in town, or tap 'No clue found'.
T.rightNone: Right. There's no clue for this one in town.
T.other: That clue goes with another promise.
T.noneHere: There's no clue for this one in town.
T.lookClue: Look again: there is a clue for this one. Here it is.

ok.notyet: Yes. It's started, but it's not done yet.
ok.ask: Yes. We can't tell yet, so we'll ask.

wrong.kept: Look again: the clue shows it's done. This promise was kept.
wrong.notyet: Look again: it's started, but not done yet. It's late, not broken.
wrong.ask: Look again: we can't tell from this. No clue doesn't mean a broken promise. We just need to ask.

T.s2: Pick a kind follow-up for each late or unclear promise. It goes in your notebook, to ask with a grown-up.

notyet.thanks: Thank you for starting. We'll check again soon.
notyet.when: When do you think it will be done?

ask.thanks: Thank you for this promise. Where can we see how it's going?
ask.why: Why is it hard to tell if it's done?
ask.when: When can we see how it's going?

T.reply: Thanks for asking kindly. You'll get an answer at the next town meeting.
T.closing: Some promises are kept, some are late, and some just need a question. Checking kindly works better than blaming.
T.can: I can check, kindly, if promises were kept.
T.tipFollow: Next time, give every late or unclear promise a kind follow-up.
T.tipAsk: Next time, remember: no clue doesn't mean a broken promise. Ask first.
T.tipStatus: Next time, read each clue slowly. Is it done, started or not clear?
T.tipClue: Next time, look all over town for each promise's clue.
T.tip100: Great watching! Try a new round. The town may take the other path.
T.real: With a grown-up, keep a 'listen and look' notebook at home. Write down changes in sounds, lights or water you notice. Never go near a building site.
T.ask: What promise in our town would you like to check on, and who could we ask?
T.guText: Promises come from the town, the builders and the neighbors. Kids match each promise to a clue a year later and choose a kind follow-up. Real checking is an adult job: ask for yearly reports and meeting minutes, and find out who enforces each promise. Each round, the town has taken one of two fair paths: building with changes, or not building while it studies.

bank.b0013: The letter says the wells were tested. The creek tests start next month.
bank.b0014: The van drives by sometimes, but no letter has come. We can't tell.
bank.b0015: We'll test the wells and the creek every month.
bank.b0016: A letter came to every farm. The wells and the creek were tested every month.
bank.b0017: We'll point every outside light down.
bank.b0018: Every outside light points down. You can see the stars over the farm.
bank.b0019: Half the lights point down. A box of new lamps waits by the fence.
bank.b0020: The lights point down, but some stay on all night. Was that part of the promise?
bank.b0021: We'll keep big trucks off Main Street.
bank.b0022: The truck sign points to the farm road. Main Street is calm.
bank.b0023: The farm road isn't finished. Some trucks still use Main Street.
bank.b0024: The sign shows a clock and a truck. Which hours does it mean?
bank.b0025: I'll teach a class for young electricians at the school.
bank.b0026: Mrs. Ana's class meets every Tuesday. Jayden is in it!
bank.b0027: The classroom is ready, but the class starts in the fall.
bank.b0028: There's a class at the school. Is it Mrs. Ana's class?
bank.b0029: We'll hold a meeting every spring to share the yearly report.
bank.b0030: The poster in the bakery window shows the date of the spring meeting.
bank.b0031: The poster is up, but the meeting has no date yet.
bank.b0032: The poster shows a meeting. Will they share the report there?
bank.b0033: We'll test the wells and the creek before we decide.
bank.b0034: A letter with the test results came to every farm.
bank.b0035: We'll pay for every study the town asks for.
bank.b0036: Study teams are measuring the field. The builders paid for every study.
bank.b0037: One study has started. The others start in the summer.
bank.b0038: Little flags stand in the field, but no one is there. Is the study still going?
bank.b0039: We'll write the new rules in open meetings.
bank.b0040: Neighbors fill Town Hall. Anyone can come and speak.
bank.b0041: The meetings were planned for winter. The first one is next month.
bank.b0042: Town Hall's lights are on. Is the meeting open to everyone?
bank.b0043: I'll start a tech club at the school.
bank.b0044: Jayden's tech club meets every Friday after school.
bank.b0045: Jayden found a room, but the club starts after the summer.
bank.b0046: Some kids meet after school. Is it Jayden's club?
bank.b0047: I'll put a poster for every town meeting in my bakery window.
bank.b0048: The bakery window shows a poster for the next meeting.
bank.b0049: Mr. Patel made the poster, but it's not in the window yet.
bank.b0050: The bakery poster is from last month. Is a new one coming?
